message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data built into this chat, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles (or any city) using a few reliable sources:

| Source | How to use it | What you’ll see |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Go to <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI value, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, O₃, NO₂, etc.), and a health‑impact summary. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Visit <https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/>. | Live AQI, historical trend graph, and forecast for the next 24 h. |
| **Weather.com** | Search “Los Angeles air quality” on the site or app. | AQI, pollutant levels, and a short health advisory. |
| **Mobile Apps** | Apps like “AirVisual”, “Plume Labs: Air Report”, or “EPA AirNow” give push notifications. | Real‑time AQI, alerts for unhealthy days, and personalized recommendations. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot right now, you can also use a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and say, “Hey Google, what’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They’ll pull the latest AQI from one of the above services.

**Quick tip:**  
- **AQI 0‑50** – Good  
- **51‑100** – Moderate  
- **101‑150** – Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups  
- **151‑200** – Unhealthy  
- **201‑300** – Very Unhealthy  
- **301‑500** – Hazardous  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into what each pollutant means or how to interpret the health advisories!
